name: Coincheck
rootCause: Unidentified assailants stole 523 million NEM coins (about $534 million) from the exchange's hot wallet. According to Coincheck, NEM coins are kept on a single-signature hot wallet instead of a more secure multi-signature wallet, and the stolen coins are confirmed to be Coincheck customers.

descriptions.text: Unidentified assailants stole 523 million NEM coins (about $534 million) from the exchange's hot wallet. According to Coincheck, NEM coins are kept on a single-signature hot wallet instead of a more secure multi-signature wallet, and the stolen coins are confirmed to be Coincheck customers.

On 26 January 2018, Coincheck's NEM (XEM) hot wallet was compromised, leading to the theft of approximately 523 million XEM (then worth ~$530 million). The attacker gained access through malware installed via a targeted phishing campaign against engineering staff, exploiting the absence of multisig and cold storage. The stolen funds were laundered quickly, resulting in minimal on-chain recovery. Coincheck reimbursed customers from corporate funds and was later acquired by Monex Group.
